summary.text: 场 is the simplified counterpart of 場. In 場, 土 marks the ground-related sense and 昜 provides the sound; the traditional graph is recorded for ritual and grain-working ground, and for broader places.

formation.text: The traditional graph 場 is phonosemantic: 土 contributes the ground-related meaning, while 昜 supplies a sound cue. 场 is used as its simplified counterpart, though the precise graphic route between the two forms remains unresolved.

components.text: In 場, 土 contributes the ground-related semantic category.
In 場, 昜 serves as the phonetic component. Its own early graphic interpretation is debated, separately from this sound role.

sound.text: In the Zhengzhang Old Chinese system, 昜 and 場 share rhyme and syllable shape, though their reconstructed initials differ. Their Middle Chinese records share the 陽 rhyme and syllable shape but have different initials; these are scholarly reconstructions and rhyme-dictionary categories.
sound.system: Old Chinese: Zhengzhang Shangfang; Middle Chinese: rhyme-dictionary categories and Baxter transcription

components.text: 场 is used in place of the traditional graph 場 in the simplified character. A proposed derivation from a cursive form has not been verified, so the exact graphic route remains unresolved.

history.text: The traditional graph 場 is analyzed as 土 plus 昜 as a sound component. A small-seal form is listed, but the cited records do not establish an oracle-bone or bronze form of 場.
塲 is recorded as a variant form of 場; it is distinct from simplified 场.
场 is the simplified counterpart of 場. The specific route, including the proposed cursive derivation, remains unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The date of 場’s earliest surviving attestation and any oracle-bone or bronze form remain undetermined. A listed small-seal image could not be inspected.
The exact graphic route from 場 to 场, including the proposed derivation from cursive writing, remains unresolved.
The earliest graphic interpretation of 昜 is debated; this is separate from its supported phonetic role in 場.

senses.text: An early dictionary account describes 場 as a way or ground for sacrificing to spirits; another account interprets it as level ground used for ancient sacrifice. The first surviving occurrence is not dated here.
The same dictionary account gives 田不耕, an uncultivated field, as an alternative gloss. Its timing relative to the ritual-ground sense is unresolved.

senses.gloss: ground for processing or drying grain
senses.text: A further gloss describes ground for grain processing, and cited texts use 場 for a grain-drying or threshing floor. The evidence does not establish when this use arose relative to the other early glosses.
Textual examples record 場 for a general place and other venues. Modern glosses include open space, field, and market, but the examples do not establish their order or semantic links.
A figurative use meaning a domain is recorded, but its date and development from a physical place are not established.
Classifier use is recorded, but its date and development from another sense are not established.

developments.text: Both senses are recorded, but a direct development from ritual ground to grain-working ground is not established.
A broadening from a specific working ground to a general place is plausible, but dates and connecting steps are not documented.
The figurative domain may extend the physical-place sense metaphorically, though the transition itself is not documented.
Classifier use is attested, but whether or how it developed from the place sense is unresolved.

limitations.text: The cited textual uses are not individually dated, so they do not provide a full semantic chronology or establish the first surviving occurrence.
The evidence supports a 土-plus-昜 phonosemantic construction; it does not support borrowing the entire graph 場 for an unrelated word.

overview.text: 场 is the simplified counterpart of 場. In 場, 土 points to ground and 昜 supplies the sound. The traditional graph is recorded for ritual and grain-working grounds, as well as broader places.

components.text: 土 points to earth or ground in the traditional character’s construction.
昜 supplies the sound cue in 場; debate about its own early picture does not change this role.
场 takes the place of 場 in the simplified graph; its specific graphic route remains unresolved.

relationships.text: 土 contributes the ground-related semantic category in traditional 場.
昜 serves as the phonetic component in traditional 場; the cited sound records support a rhyme and syllable-shape correspondence.
场 is the graphic substitute used in the simplified character for the 土-plus-昜 traditional graph 場; its precise historical route remains unresolved.
